question:
After each change to a system, how should the team decide what to test again, and at which point of the process?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).
answer:
[JEV filter] kept 12 of 12 guidelines (JEV 'lenient' score > 0.5)

# Guidelines
- Define regression testing as selective retesting: after each change, selectively retest the system [SWEBOK excerpt 021f9937eefeac172cee] system still complies with its specified requirements. (source: root/Software Testing Levels, Objectives, and Approaches/Alpha, Beta, and Regression Testing Procedures.md) [JEV 0.95]
- Apply regression testing at every test level (unit, integration, system, etc.) — not just at the system level — so that each layer of the system is verified after a change. (source: root/Software Testing Levels, Objectives, and Approaches/Alpha, Beta, and Regression Testing Procedures.md) [JEV 0.92]
- Balance thoroughness against cost: make a conscious trade-off between the assurance given by running the full regression suite [SWEBOK excerpt a214e00aef99bf34a85f], since retesting everything can be very time-consuming. (source: root/Software Testing Levels, Objectives, and Approaches/Alpha, Beta, and Regression Testing Procedures.md) [JEV 0.97]
- Use test-case selection, minimisation, and prioritisation on the existing test suite to decide which tests to run after a change, rather than blindly re-running all tests. (source: root/Software Testing Levels, Objectives, and Approaches/Regression Testing in Software Development.md) [JEV 0.96]
- Include both functional and non-functional retesting (reliability, accessibility, usability, maintainability, conversion, migration, compatibility) in the regression effort after a change. (source: root/Software Testing Levels, Objectives, and Approaches/Regression Testing in Software Development.md) [JEV 0.95]
- Perform regression testing [SWEBOK excerpt 0f6027292d0f7e6a203b]: this is the standard placement of regression testing in the process pipeline. (source: root/Software Testing Levels, Objectives, and Approaches/Regression Testing in Software Development.md) [JEV 0.98]
- Treat regression testing as a core [SWEBOK excerpt 6848235a3dbbf75898e4] processes, since all of these paradigms rely on it after every change. (source: root/Software Testing Levels, Objectives, and Approaches/Regression Testing in Software Development.md) [JEV 0.92]
- Prioritise test cases by scheduling those most likely to detect faults first, and use similarity-based (or dissimilarity-based) heuristics [SWEBOK excerpt c5ce46e06ec01d7341a5], code coverage, and system reliability. (source: root/Software Testing Levels, Objectives, and Approaches/Test Case Prioritization for Fault Detection.md; root/Software Testing Levels, Objectives, and Approaches/Non-Functional Testing and Test Case Prioritization/Non-functional Testing and Dissimilarity-Based Test Prioritization.md) [JEV 0.92]
- In shift-left development (Agile, DevOps, TDD), make regression, security, and privacy the primary internal-code-quality objectives after each change, targeting unit and integration testing levels using structure-based testing techniques. (source: root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Testing Across Development Processes and Domains/Testing Aspects in Shift-Left Development.md) [JEV 0.93]
- Adopt continuous testing — [SWEBOK excerpt 0fff44da6611d2ddd930] development lifecycle — to evaluate quality at every step of the [SWEBOK excerpt d7e57d9d89af6c96b337]. (source: root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Maintenance, Evolution, and Quality Assurance/Continuous Integration, Delivery, and Software Maintenance/Continuous Delivery and Testing in Software Development.md) [JEV 0.97]
- Use Continuous Integration (CI) with automated builds that include automated testing so that every integration of a team member's change is verified immediately, detecting integration errors as quickly as possible. (source: root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Maintenance, Evolution, and Quality Assurance/Continuous Integration, Delivery, and Software Maintenance/Continuous Integration and DevOps Practices/Continuous Integration, Delivery, Testing and Deployment.md; root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Maintenance, Evolution, and Quality Assurance/Continuous Integration, Delivery, and Software Maintenance/Continuous Integration and DevOps Practices/Continuous Integration Goals and Automated Processes.md) [JEV 0.97]
- Adopt the shift-left principle: promote testing in the early stages of development after each change [SWEBOK excerpt f84aa3f3eb8164edfdd3], increasing overall quality and reducing the cost and risk of late-stage testing. (source: root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Testing Across Development Processes and Domains/Unified Process Phases and Shift-Left Testing Movement.md) [JEV 0.97]
